title: Circuit research file (schema_version 1)
description: One file per circuit on the 2026 calendar, written by tools/track/research/build_research_pack.py. All distances are metres and all positions are WGS84 latitude/longitude, so the files do not depend on the scene frame. A track builder converts to the scene frame itself (see README.md). Rule for every field: a value that could not be checked against a source is null, and a nearby 'note' says why. Numbers are never guessed.

note.description: Plain-English explanation, usually why a value is null or how it was worked out.

source_ref.description: Id of an entry in the top-level 'sources' list (wikipedia, fia_map, fia_notes, osm, tumftm, dem) or a short text.

s_m.description: Distance in metres along the pack centreline (cad/track/raw/centreline/<id>.csv), measured in race direction from s = 0.

side.description: Side of the track, looking in race direction.

fia_location.description: Location text copied from the FIA circuit map, e.g. '110m after T10'. Turn numbers follow the FIA map.

id.description: Short id, same as the file name and the id in calendar_2026.json.

status.description: 'confirmed' when the round is on the official calendar.

weekend.description: ISO date range 'YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD' (local dates at the circuit).

layout.description: Name of the layout used in F1 (from the Wikipedia infobox).

length.description: Lap length. 'official_m' is the FIA centreline length from the circuit map. 'checks' lists every length found so a builder can see how well the sources agree.

osm_loop_m.description: Length of the closed loop found in the OpenStreetMap circuit ways.

pack_centreline_m.description: Length of the centreline CSV in this pack.

turns.description: FIA turn number or range, e.g. '10-11'.

basis.description: How the race direction of the centreline was decided.

lap_record.description: Race lap record for the current layout as listed on Wikipedia. All fields null when none is listed.

centreline.description: The track centreline in race direction. The CSV columns are s_m, lat, lon, elev_m, w_right_m, w_left_m, one row every spacing_m metres. Width columns are blank when there is no TUMFTM data.

source.description: tumftm = TUMFTM file fitted onto OSM; osm = OSM circuit ways only.

s0.description: Where s = 0 is. Not exactly the start/finish line.

tumftm.description: The TUMFTM file and how it was fitted: origin_lat/origin_lon is where the TUMFTM (0, 0) point lands, rotation_deg turns TUMFTM x/y (east/north-ish) onto true east/north, georef_median_m and georef_p95_m say how closely it matches OSM. 'used' is false when the file holds an older layout.

osm.description: OSM relation id or list of way ids used for the loop.

elevation.description: Height along the centreline from a public terrain model (OpenTopoData). These are computed, not official.

total_change_m.description: Highest minus lowest point after smoothing.

total_climb_per_lap_m.description: Sum of all uphill gains over one lap after smoothing.

kerbs.description: value stays null (no source publishes kerbs as data). fia_changes quotes FIA Race Director note lines that mention kerbs.

run_off.description: value stays null. fia_changes quotes FIA lines about gravel, asphalt, grass, walls and barriers. osm_hints totals what OSM has mapped near the track (surface areas in m2 within 60 m, barrier lengths in m within 30 m).

track_limits.description: Track limits text from the FIA Race Director notes.

length_m.description: OSM pit lane way length, usually including entry and exit roads. Not official.

fia_entry_exit_rules.description: Pit entry and exit section quoted from the FIA notes.

sectors.description: Timing sectors from the FIA circuit map: sector lengths, intermediate points and the speed trap.

overtaking.description: 2026 rounds: straight mode zones (normal-grip and low-grip activation points) and the overtake mode detection/activation points, from the 2026 FIA map. Rounds without a 2026 map yet: the 2025 DRS detection and activation points.

landmarks.description: Grandstands, bridges, tunnels and the largest named buildings from OSM near the track, each with s_m, side and distance from the centreline. 'named' lists features mentioned in the Wikipedia article, without positions.

gaps.description: Plain list of what is missing or uncertain for this circuit.

built.description: Present when a scene for this circuit already exists in the repo (only the Red Bull Ring today).
